insight.title: Why a Full Calendar Is a Hidden Risk
insight.subtitle: How leaving empty space in your day protects you from unexpected problems

sections.text: Nature never builds a tree with just enough wood to stand. It builds for the once-in-a-decade storm. A healthy forest keeps a surplus of energy hidden, ready for a crisis that hasn't happened yet.

We mistake "empty" for "wasted." Your body doesn't have just enough blood to survive; it has a massive surplus. In biological systems, efficiency is a weakness that leads to collapse during a single shock.
When you schedule every minute, you remove your insurance. You aren't being productive; you are building a system that breaks the moment a single meeting runs over or an unexpected crisis arrives.
Try this today: When you look at your calendar today, leave thirty minutes completely blank to absorb the unexpected.
The strongest systems in the world are never the ones running at one hundred percent capacity.
